decision: The three declaration drafts under docs/tier4_orchestration_state/msca_dn/declarations/ were re-rendered by their own tool, py -3.10 -m tools.draft_fidelity_declarations. Their bytes changed, and the two sha256 values the 2026-10-08 approval record pinned for the JSON drafts no longer describe the files. The new hashes are recorded below.
why: The drafts carry an adoption-cost scan that is deliberately coupled to the repository tree: it measures every committed artifact that would have to be re-recorded or explained if a declaration were adopted. Any new artifact that names a register therefore makes the drafts stale, and their tool's --check exits 1. The 2026-10-08 approval record recognised this for the Markdown checklist and pinned no hash for it, giving the reason in the record. The same reasoning applies to the two JSON drafts, which carry the same scan output under referenced_by_path; pinning their hashes bound a measurement to a tree that was certain to grow.

the_cycle_and_how_it_is_cut.problem: A record that explains a re-render by naming a register path is itself picked up by the next scan, so writing the explanation makes the drafts stale again.
the_cycle_and_how_it_is_cut.rule: This record cites the drafts by path and names no register path and no register hash, so the hashes it states stay the committed hashes without a further re-render. A record may name a register — the R05 successor-dispositions record does, in a command it quotes — but then its own commit must re-render the drafts afterwards. Either way the invariant is the same: a stated hash describes the committed bytes.
